polls.note: Quaest national poll released on 21/Oct, registration BR-08535/2026, 2,154 in-person interviews with voters aged 16 or over from 17 to 20/Oct, margin of 2pp at 95% confidence (G1, O Globo and Valor). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 45% AND LULA 44% in total votes, with 9% blank, null or not voting. In the 10 to 13/Oct wave it was 46% and 44%. 52% would not vote for Flávio Bolsonaro and 47% would not vote for Lula. The Lula government is disapproved by 47% and approved by 46%.

Ideia for Canal Meio, national poll released on 21/Oct, registration BR-08251/2026, 1,500 telephone interviews from 15 to 19/Oct, margin of 2.5pp at 95% confidence (Estadão, O Globo and CNN Brasil). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 48% AND LULA 46% in total votes; in valid votes, 51.1% to 48.9%. It is the pollster's first national poll after the first round; in the one of 30/Sep, the second-round simulation gave 48.5% to Lula and 48% to Flávio Bolsonaro.

Palver national poll released on 21/Oct, registration BR-04612/2026, 5,000 online interviews from 18 to 20/Oct according to the releases (the TSE registration lists fieldwork from 16 to 20/Oct), non-probability sample recruited through ads, margin of 2.4pp at 95% confidence (Congresso em Foco and Times Brasil). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 50% AND LULA 48% in total votes, with 1% blank, null or not voting; in valid votes, 51% to 49%. In the 10 to 13/Oct wave it was 50% and 49%. 49% would not vote for Lula and 47% would not vote for Flávio Bolsonaro. The Lula government is disapproved by 51% and approved by 48%.

Futura/100% Cidades national poll released on 21/Oct, registration BR-06614/2026, 2,000 voters by telephone on 19 and 20/Oct, margin of 2.2pp at 95% confidence (Rádio Itatiaia, Rádio Corredor and TradeMap). It is the first national poll with its entire fieldwork after the Band debate of 18/Oct. ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 48.9% AND LULA 46.8% in total votes, with 2% blank, null or for neither and 2.3% who do not know; in valid votes, 51.1% to 48.9%. In the 16 and 17/Oct wave it was 48.3% to 47.5% in total votes.

Veritá national poll released on 21/Oct, registration BR-06396/2026, 15,554 voters from 15 to 19/Oct, margin of 1pp at 95% confidence, self-funded (Jornal Razão, R7 and CNN Brasil). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 49.7% AND LULA 48.2% in total votes (R7); in valid votes, 50.7% to 49.3% (CNN Brasil). In the 12 to 16/Oct wave, released only in valid votes, it was 51.1% to 48.9%.

Alfa Inteligência national poll released on 20/Oct, registration BR-00820/2026, 2,700 voters in in-person interviews from 15 to 19/Oct, margin of 1.9pp at 95% confidence, self-funded (UOL, Estadão and CNN Brasil). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 48.8% AND LULA 45.9% in total votes, with 3.5% blank, null or for neither and 1.8% who do not know; in valid votes, 51.5% to 48.5%. In the spontaneous question, 47% to 43%. 46% would not vote for Lula under any circumstances and 45% would not vote for Flávio Bolsonaro, and the Lula government is disapproved by 50% and approved by 46%. It is the pollster's first national poll after the first round; in the one of 24/Sep, the second-round simulation was 43% to 43%.

Real Time Big Data national poll released on 20/Oct, registration BR-02952/2026, 2,000 voters interviewed by telephone across the national territory from 15 to 19/Oct, margin of 2pp at 95% confidence (CNN Brasil, CartaCapital and Metrópoles). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 48% AND LULA 45% in total votes, with 5% blank or null and 2% who do not know; in valid votes, 52% to 48%. 35% reject Lula and 33% Flávio Bolsonaro. It is the pollster's first national poll after the first round; in the one of 01/Oct, the second-round simulation gave 46% to Flávio Bolsonaro and 45% to Lula.

AtlasIntel national poll released on 19/Oct, commissioned by Bloomberg, registration BR-02418/2026, 4,998 voters through random digital recruitment from 13 to 18/Oct, margin of 1pp at 95% confidence (Estadão, Brasil de Fato and Money Times). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 49.8% AND LULA 47.6% in total votes; in valid votes, 51.1% to 48.9% (Poder360). In the 03 to 08/Oct wave it was 51.1% to 45.7% in total votes and 52.8% to 47.2% in valid votes. The Lula government is disapproved by 52.3% and approved by 46.2%.

BTG/Nexus national poll released on 19/Oct, registration BR-04499/2026, 2,002 voters by telephone from 16 to 18/Oct, margin of 2pp at 95% confidence, commissioned by the bank BTG Pactual (Estadão, Congresso em Foco and UOL). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 46.5% AND LULA 45.9% in total votes; in valid votes, 50.3% to 49.7%, and in the spontaneous question 44.5% each. In the 10 to 12/Oct wave it was 48% to 45% in total votes and 52% to 48% in valid votes. 47.8% would not vote for Lula under any circumstances and 46.8% would not vote for Flávio Bolsonaro, and the Lula government is disapproved by 48.8% and approved by 47.2%.

Futura/100% Cidades national poll released on 19/Oct, registration BR-06715/2026, 2,000 voters by telephone on 16 and 17/Oct, margin of 2.2pp at 95% confidence (Money Times). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 48.3% AND LULA 47.5% in total votes, with 2.4% blank or null and 1.9% who do not know; in valid votes, 50.4% to 49.6% (Money Times and CNN Brasil). In the wave released on 16/Oct it was 49% to 47.5% in total votes.

PoderData national poll released on 19/Oct in partnership with Aya, registration BR-02586/2026, 3,000 automated telephone interviews in 695 municipalities from 16 to 18/Oct, margin of 1.8pp at 95% confidence (Poder360, UOL and Exame). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 52% AND LULA 48% OF THE VALID VOTES; Poder360, which publishes the poll, released only the valid votes, and so this entry has no second-round pair. UOL published 49% to 46% in total votes. In the 13 to 15/Oct wave it was a tie at 50% of the valid votes. 48% would not vote for Lula under any circumstances and 44% would not vote for Flávio Bolsonaro.

DataTrends national poll released on 19/Oct, registration BR-04454/2026, 2,000 voters from all 27 federative units in automated telephone interviews from 15 to 17/Oct, margin of 2.19pp at 95% confidence (the Edmar Lyra and Mário Flávio blogs). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 51.5% AND LULA 48.5% OF THE VALID VOTES; the release does not include total votes, and so this entry has no second-round pair. In the 07 to 09/Oct wave it was 53.1% to 46.9% in valid votes.

Vox Brasil national poll released on 18/Oct, registration BR-04332/2026, 2,100 voters aged 16 or over in in-person household interviews from 15 to 17/Oct, margin of 2.15pp at 95% confidence, R$ 50 thousand from own funds (Poder360, Sul 21 and Metrópoles). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND LULA HAS 46.4% AND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO 44.6% in total votes, within the margin, with 5% none, blank or null and 3.9% who do not know; in valid votes, 51% to 49%, and in the spontaneous question 50.6% to 49.4% of the valid votes. In the 05 to 07/Oct wave it was 44.2% to 42.7%. 46.9% think Lula wins and 41.6% bet on Flávio Bolsonaro. Fieldwork ended before the Band debate of 18/Oct.

Ipespe national poll released on 17/Oct, second wave of the Ipespe/Abrapel Campaign Tracking in the second round, registration BR-00223/2026, 1,500 voters aged 16 or over by phone from 13 to 15/Oct, margin of 2.6pp at 95.45% confidence (Exame, O Globo and Metrópoles). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 48% AND LULA 46% in total votes, with 3% blank and null votes and 3% who do not know or did not answer; in valid votes, 51.2% to 48.8% (CNN Brasil and Poder360). In the 06 to 08/Oct wave it was 49% to 44%. In the spontaneous question, 47% to 44%. 47% would not vote for Flávio Bolsonaro under any circumstances and another 47% would not vote for Lula; 47% say they would certainly vote for Flávio Bolsonaro and 45% for Lula.

Veritá national poll released on 17/Oct, registration BR-01107/2026, 15,554 voters from 12 to 16/Oct, margin of 1pp at 95% confidence, own funds (CNN Brasil); the pollster uses automated phone interviews and builds its national estimate from state surveys (Exame). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 51.1% OF THE VALID VOTES AND LULA 48.9%; the release does not include total votes, so this entry has no second-round pair and does not enter the divergence chart. It is the pollster's first national poll after the first round.

Gerp national poll released on the night of 16/Oct, with release registered with the TSE for 13/Oct, before fieldwork, registration BR-05187/2026, 2,400 voters by phone from 14 to 16/Oct, margin of 2pp at 95% confidence (Poder360 and Gazeta do Povo). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 50% AND LULA 45% in total votes, with 3% who do not know; in valid votes, 52% to 48%. In the 08 to 12/Oct wave it was 53% to 44% in total votes. In the spontaneous question, 49% to 44%. 49% reject Lula and 46% reject Flávio Bolsonaro, and the Lula government is disapproved by 48% and approved by 46% (CNN Brasil).

CNT/MDA national poll released on 16/Oct, commissioned by the Confederação Nacional do Transporte, registration BR-00652/2026, 2,002 in-person interviews in the 27 federative units from 13 to 15/Oct, margin of 2.2pp at 95% confidence (Metrópoles and Gazeta do Povo; Gazeta do Povo reports 2,014 respondents). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 46.8% AND LULA 45.9% in the prompted question, with 4.9% blank and null votes and 2.4% undecided; in valid votes, 50.5% to 49.5%. In the spontaneous question, 45.6% to 44.1%. In the 03/Oct wave, on the eve of the first round, the pollster's second-round scenario gave Lula 47.3% and Flávio Bolsonaro 43.1%. The Lula government is rated negatively by 39.5% and positively by 37.8%, against 41% and 35% on 03/Oct, and 49.3% disapprove of Lula's personal performance and 47.7% approve (Metrópoles).

Futura/100% Cidades national poll released on 16/Oct, registration BR-03764/2026, 2,000 voters aged 16 or over by phone, fieldwork on 14 and 15/Oct according to the reports (the registration lists 13 to 15/Oct), margin of 2.2pp at 95% confidence, R$ 160 thousand (Poder360, CNN Brasil and Money Times). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 49% AND LULA 47.5% in total votes, with 1.5% blank, null or none and 2.1% who do not know; in valid votes, 50.8% to 49.2%. In the 13/Oct wave it was 50% to 46.6% in total votes and 51.8% to 48.2% in valid votes. 47.2% reject Lula and 46.1% reject Flávio Bolsonaro (Poder360).

PoderData national poll released on 16/Oct in partnership with Aya, registration BR-04258/2026, 3,000 automated phone interviews in 644 municipalities across the 27 federative units from 13 to 15/Oct, margin of 1.8pp at 95% confidence, own funds (Poder360). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO AND LULA HAVE 50% OF THE VALID VOTES EACH; the release does not include total votes, so this entry has no second-round pair. In valid votes, it was 51% to 49% for Flávio Bolsonaro in the 10 to 12/Oct wave and 53% to 47% in the 05 to 07/Oct wave. 46% would not vote for Lula under any circumstances and 45% would not vote for Flávio Bolsonaro (Poder360 and Hora do Povo). 51% think Flávio Bolsonaro has the better chance of winning and 42% bet on Lula, and the Lula government is disapproved by 47% and approved by 46%.

Datafolha national poll released on 15/Oct, commissioned by Folha de S.Paulo, registration BR-00466/2026, 2,520 voters aged 16 or over interviewed in person from 13 to 15/Oct, margin of 2pp at 95% confidence (Metrópoles, CNN Brasil and Gazeta do Povo). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 47% AND LULA 45%, after 49% to 45% in the pollster's 08/Oct wave; blank, null and none add up to 6% and undecided 2%. In valid votes, Flávio Bolsonaro 51% and Lula 49%, against 52% and 48% on 08/Oct. Rejection: 46% would not vote for Lula and 44% would not vote for Flávio Bolsonaro. The Lula government is rated negatively by 41% and positively by 35% (Folha de S.Paulo).

Palver national poll released on 15/Oct, the pollster's first after the first round, registration BR-08028/2026, 5,000 interviews from 10 to 13/Oct, margin of 2.3pp at 95% confidence, R$ 30 thousand paid with its own funds (Poder360). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 50% AND LULA 49%, with 1% blank and null votes and no undecided voters. In the 03/Oct wave, on the eve of the first round, it was 49% and 44%.

Indexa national poll released on 15/Oct, commissioned by Estadão/Broadcast, registration BR-04629/2026, 2,000 interviews on 13 and 14/Oct, margin of 2.2pp at 95% confidence, R$ 164 thousand (Poder360 and Estadão). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 44% AND LULA 42% in total votes, with 8% who say they will not vote, 4% blank and null votes and 2% undecided; in valid votes, 51% to 49%. In the 30/Sep wave, still before the first round, it was 42% for Flávio Bolsonaro and 43% for Lula. The same wave measured 60% in favour of ending the 6x1 work schedule and 30% against, and 50% disapproval of the Lula government.

Quaest national poll released on 14/Oct, the pollster's first after the first round, registration BR-08729/2026, 2,154 in-person interviews with voters aged 16 or older from 10 to 13/Oct, margin of 2pp with 95% confidence, commissioned by Grupo Globo (Metrópoles, Exame and O Globo). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 46% AND LULA 44% in total votes, with 9% blank and spoiled ballots and 1% undecided. In the 03/Oct wave it was 44% and 42%.

PoderData national poll released on 13/Oct in partnership with Aya, registration BR-01209/2026, 3,000 automated phone interviews from 10 to 12/Oct, margin of 1.8pp with 95% confidence (Jovem Pan and Poder360). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 48% AND LULA 46% in total votes, with 5% blank and spoiled ballots and 2% who could not answer; in valid votes, 51% to 49%. In the 05 to 07/Oct wave it was 49% to 44% in total votes. 46% say they would not vote for Lula under any circumstances and 44% for Flávio Bolsonaro. The Lula government is disapproved by 50% and approved by 44%.

BTG/Nexus national poll released on 13/Oct, the pollster's first after the first round, registration BR-07997/2026, 2,002 voters by phone from 10 to 12/Oct, margin of 2pp with 95% confidence, commissioned by the bank BTG Pactual (Jovem Pan and CNN Brasil). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 48% AND LULA 45% in total votes, with 5% blank and spoiled ballots and 2% undecided; in valid votes, 52% to 48%. 51% say they would not vote for Lula under any circumstances and 47% for Flávio Bolsonaro. The Lula government is disapproved by 50% and approved by 45%.

Futura/100% Cidades national poll released on 13/Oct, registration BR-00650/2026, 2,000 voters aged 16 or over by phone from 07 to 10/Oct, margin of 2.2pp with 95% confidence (Transmissão Política, Exame and CNN Brasil). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 50% AND LULA 46.6% in total votes, with 1.7% blank, spoiled or none and 1.7% who don't know; in valid votes, 51.8% to 48.2%. 48.6% reject Lula and 45.4% reject Flávio Bolsonaro (CNN Brasil).

Gerp national poll released on the night of 12/Oct, with release registered with the TSE for 13/Oct, registration BR-07877/2026, 2,400 voters by phone on 08, 09 and 12/Oct, margin of 2pp with 95.55% confidence, with its own funds (CNN Brasil, Conexão Política and TMC). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 53% AND LULA 44% in total votes, with 3% who don't know or didn't answer and 1% who would vote for neither; in valid votes, 55% to 45%. The Lula government is disapproved by 49% and approved by 45% (Jovem Pan).

DataTrends national poll released on 11/Oct, the pollster's first in the second round, registration BR-03576/2026, 2,000 voters in automated phone interviews from 07 to 09/Oct, margin of 2.19pp with 95% confidence, R$ 25 thousand from its own funds (Poder360, Diário de São Paulo and GP1). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 50% AND LULA 44% in total votes, with 5% blank and spoiled ballots and 1% who don't know or didn't answer; in valid votes, 53.1% to 46.9%. The Lula government is disapproved by 53% and approved by 45% (Blog Edmar Lyra).

Ipespe national poll released on 10/Oct, the first wave of the Ipespe/Abrapel Campaign Tracking in the second round, registration BR-00933/2026, 1,500 voters through random digital recruitment from 06 to 08/Oct, margin of 2.6pp with 95.45% confidence (O Globo and Exame). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 49% AND LULA 44% in total votes, with 5% blank and spoiled ballots and 3% who don't know or didn't answer. In valid votes, Flávio Bolsonaro 52.7% and Lula 47.3%, a calculation the pollster calls an exercise. Among Augusto Cury's voters, Flávio Bolsonaro has 50% and Lula 29%; among Ronaldo Caiado's, 56% to 15%, and the pollster warns that these groups are small in the sample. 47% say they would certainly vote for Flávio Bolsonaro and 46% that they would not vote for him under any circumstances; for Lula, 43% and 49%.

AtlasIntel national poll released on 09/Oct, commissioned by Bloomberg, the pollster's first after the first round, registration BR-03663/2026, 5,026 voters through random digital recruitment from 03 to 08/Oct, margin of 1pp with 95% confidence (Estadão, CNN Brasil and CartaCapital). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 51.1% AND LULA 45.7% in total votes, and blank ballots, spoiled ballots and undecided voters add up to 3.2%, after 47.6% to 47.4% for Lula in the pollster's round of 03/Oct, conducted before the vote. In valid votes, Flávio Bolsonaro 52.8% and Lula 47.2%. Among Augusto Cury's voters, Lula has 50.4% and Flávio Bolsonaro 38.9%; among Ronaldo Caiado's, Flávio Bolsonaro has 54.9% and Lula 26.9%.

Vox Brasil national poll released on 09/Oct, the pollster's first after the first round, registration BR-09623/2026, 2,100 voters interviewed in person from 05 to 07/Oct, margin of 2.15pp with 95% confidence (CartaCapital, CNN Brasil and Poder360). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND LULA HAS 44.2% AND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO 42.7%, within the margin, with 3.4% blank and spoiled ballots and 9.7% who do not know, after 48.2% to 45.2% for Flávio Bolsonaro in the pollster's round of 02/Oct, conducted before the vote. In valid votes, Lula 50.86% and Flávio Bolsonaro 49.14%. 76.2% of voters say they are fully decided.

Datafolha national poll released on 08/Oct, the pollster's first after the first round, registration BR-02949/2026, 2,520 voters aged 16 or older interviewed from 06 to 08/Oct, margin of 2pp with 95% confidence (Brasil de Fato, CartaCapital, G1 and Valor). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 49% AND LULA 45%, after 47% to 46% for Lula in the pollster's round of 03/Oct, conducted before the vote; blank, null and none add up to 5% and undecided 1%. In valid votes, Flávio Bolsonaro 52% and Lula 48%. Rejection: 46% would not vote for Lula and 43% would not vote for Flávio Bolsonaro. The Lula government's rating is negative for 40% and positive for 35%.

PoderData national poll released on 08/Oct in partnership with Aya, the first poll published after the first round, registration BR-08134/2026, 3,000 telephone interviews in 705 municipalities across the 27 federative units, from 05 to 07/Oct, margin of 1.8pp with 95% confidence (Poder360 and Jovem Pan). ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 49% AND LULA 44% in total votes, with 5% blank and spoiled ballots and 2% undecided; in valid votes, 53% to 47%. Among Augusto Cury's voters, Flávio Bolsonaro has 56% and Lula 27%; among Ronaldo Caiado's, 57% to 19%; among Renan Santos's, 48% to 25%; among Romeu Zema's, 72% to 10% (Jovem Pan). On expectation of victory, 54% think Flávio Bolsonaro wins and 37% that Lula wins. Rejection: 46% would not vote for Lula and 43% would not vote for Flávio Bolsonaro (CNN Brasil). 📌 Correction of 09/Oct: on 08/Oct this entry said the release included only valid votes; it also included the total, which has been added here.

Palver national poll released on 03/Oct, the pollster's sixth round, registration BR-00198/2026, 5,000 participants recruited online between 30/Sep and 03/Oct, non-probability sample calibrated with IBGE data, the second round of 2022 and the TSE party membership registry, maximum margin of 2.4pp at 95% confidence (Exame). ⭐ IN THE FIRST ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 47% AND LULA 43%, after 44% to 44% in the pollster's round of 29/Sep, with Renan Santos at 7%, Augusto Cury and Ronaldo Caiado at 1% and Romeu Zema below 1%. ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 49% AND LULA 44%, after 47% to 45% on 29/Sep. Lula beats Augusto Cury by 44% to 36%, Renan Santos by 44% to 33%, Romeu Zema by 44% to 42% and Ronaldo Caiado by 43% to 42%.

AtlasIntel national poll released on the night of 03/Oct (Exame, 22h00 BRT), commissioned by Bloomberg, registration BR-00999/2026, 4,945 voters through random digital recruitment between 27/Sep and 02/Oct, margin of 1pp with 95% confidence. ⭐ IN TOTAL FIRST-ROUND VOTES LULA HAS 46.7% AND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO 43.8%, after 45.3% to 42.2% in the pollster's 29/Sep round, with Renan Santos at 4.6%, Augusto Cury at 2.1% and Ronaldo Caiado at 1.4%. In valid votes, Lula 47% and Flávio Bolsonaro 44.1%. ⚖️ IN THE SECOND ROUND LULA HAS 47.6% AND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO 47.4% in total votes, and 50.1% to 49.9% in valid votes, after 47.7% to 47.6% for Flávio Bolsonaro on 29/Sep.

Gerp's second national poll released on 03/Oct, registration BR-08168/2026, 2,400 voters by phone between 01 and 03/Oct, margin of 2pp (Jovem Pan). The pollster reports that the measurements of 2 and 3/Oct share part of the interviews with round BR-00509/2026. ⭐ IN THE FIRST ROUND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO HAS 44% AND LULA 42%, after 43% to 41% in the previous measurement, with Ronaldo Caiado at 4%, Augusto Cury at 3%, Renan Santos at 2% and Romeu Zema at 1%. In valid votes, Flávio Bolsonaro 45% and Lula 43%. This round's second-round numbers were not checked in the body and stay out.

Datafolha national poll released on 03/Oct, registration BR-01708/2026, 4,006 voters aged 16 or older interviewed on 03/Oct, margin of 2pp at 95% confidence (Money Times and Valor). ⭐ IN THE FIRST ROUND LULA HAS 42% AND FLÁVIO BOLSONARO 40%, after 42% to 38% in the pollster's round released on 01/Oct, with Ronaldo Caiado at 4%, Renan Santos and Augusto Cury at 3% and Romeu Zema below 1%; blank, null and none total 4% and undecided 3%.
